questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle tailgaters?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by encouraging them to follow at the higher speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes turn signals hard to see, the rider should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk the horn to warn other drivers of turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly communicate with other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you properly, meaning:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing.
Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits properly when your feet can comfortably reach the ground while you are seated. Make sure the motorcycle fits you before riding.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip is to:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, limit riding time each day and take frequent breaks to rest. Avoid stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If a hazard appears, you will have more time to respond and more room to move safely.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chance of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.

questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, be visible, signal clearly, maintain safe space, look ahead, and identify hazards. Always be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue while riding?
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks on long trips to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may seem to help but can make you extremely tired when it wears off, making riding more dangerous. Dress warmly and use a windshield to help prevent fatigue from weather.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings?

options.text: Speed up to cross them faster.
Zigzag to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, maintain a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to correct the weave by zigzagging is more dangerous and makes it harder to stay in your lane.

questions.question: What mirror must all motorcycles have?

options.text: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar.
A rearview mirror on the right handlebar.
A rearview mirror only if the rider is under 21.

questions.correctAnswerText: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar.
questions.explanation: Tennessee law requires all motorcycles to have a rearview mirror mounted on the left handlebar in an upright position.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important factor when buying a helmet. Choose one that fastens securely, fits correctly, and has a DOT certification.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of you, which lane position is safest?
questions.explanation: The best lane position depends on traffic and road conditions. When vehicles are on both sides of you, the center position is usually the safest.

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?
questions.explanation: The safest lane position changes based on traffic and road conditions. Adjust your position as needed.

questions.question: How can other drivers see you better?
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing to make it easier for other drivers to see you. This works both day and night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic rules apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding to help other drivers see you, even during the day.

questions.question: When using saddlebags to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
Unevenly distribute weight into the saddlebags.
Place as much weight as possible into one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
questions.explanation: Put equal weight in each saddlebag. Uneven weight can cause the motorcycle to drift to one side.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as you would if riding during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
Ride faster than you would if riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know. Slower speeds give you more time to avoid hazards when visibility is poor.

questions.question: When a tailgater follows you, you should:

options.text: Not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. The motorcycle responds more slowly with extra weight, so it needs more time to slow down and turn. Start slowing down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have increased control of their motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to lose control. The motorcycle may go into another lane or off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
Clothing of any color because other drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Darkly-colored clothing to contrast with the bright sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other food and drink. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream and reaches the brain quickly.
